reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous pattern recognition with empirical explanation tools to identify shared spurious features. It leverages direct observation of commonalities across instances to form hypotheses, then validates them using reliable XAI methods that quantify feature importance and attribution. This ensures both reasoning efficiency and statistical rigor in detecting spurious correlations.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 27362) and evaluate their semantic relevance to income class prediction.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: List of shared features across all three instances with a note on their semantic plausibility for predicting income class

autonomous_tasks.query: Why might a shared feature like 'Married-civ-spouse' or 'Husband' be spurious, even if it appears in all instances? Consider whether it correlates with high income without causal or semantic justification.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Hypothesis on why a shared feature may be spurious despite being common

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides robust, model-agnostic feature importance scores that can highlight which features have high attribution despite lacking semantic relevance. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer complementary local and global interpretations, helping to confirm whether key features drive predictions incorrectly. Sensitivity analysis quantifies the effect of removing features, validating their spuriousness by showing whether prediction outcomes degrade significantly when those features are ablated. Together, these tools detect and validate shared spurious patterns across instances.
